body: A plan's `ci.py conclusion --wait {s}` entry is a bound, not a verdict: when the run outlasts it the read prints `verdict: in progress` with the oldest job still running, which is neither green nor red, and the operator pass has to fire the read again once the run completes. The CI wall grows as checks are added (the `Stand checks repeated` job, which runs every `stand_*` target three times, is the oldest job at the bound), so a wait copied from an earlier plan falls behind. Set the next plan's wait above the latest measured wall the previous operator pass recorded (its `ci.py conclusion` line prints `wall {n} s`), with margin, rather than carrying the old figure forward.

body_fields.rule: Props of a component alone are given as a maker run once in the mount's root scope, never as a value.
body_fields.why: An EventHandler prop can only be made inside a Dioxus runtime.
body_fields.because: A props-value signature was replaced by a props maker because a value cannot carry an EventHandler made outside a runtime.

body_fields.name: Root context of a component alone provided before the build
body_fields.rule: A root context for a component alone is provided on the mount before the harness builds.
body_fields.why: A context added after the build reaches no render.
body_fields.because: A boot that provided TimerTicks after the build was replaced since the context reached no render, which binds every caller of the mount.

body_fields.name: Pinned viewport read from the document
body_fields.rule: A boot-condition check of the pinned viewport reads the document viewport, never the root element's bounds.
body_fields.why: A component alone has no shell CSS, so its root element sizes to its content.
body_fields.because: The root element of a component alone was measured at its content height, so only the document viewport reads the pinned size.

body_fields.name: Harness graph unit tests turn accessibility on
body_fields.rule: A harness unit test of the UI graph turns the accessibility feature on through its dev-dependency, for the test build only.
body_fields.why: A per-package test build leaves the accessibility feature off, and the UI graph is gated by it.
body_fields.because: The harness's first unit test reads the UI graph, which a per-package test build compiles out unless the dev-dependency turns the feature on.

body_fields.name: Timer context checked by delivered ticks
body_fields.rule: A check that the Timer's TimerTicks context is present reads delivered ticks, never the Timer's elapsed text at boot.
body_fields.why: The Timer falls back to wall time without the context, so its elapsed text at boot reads the same either way.
body_fields.because: The planned check by elapsed text at boot could not fail, so the check of the context reads delivered ticks instead.
